user.title: Set up ISDT Device
user.description: Confirm the detected ISDT device to add it to Home Assistant.

bluetooth_confirm.title: Confirm detected device
bluetooth_confirm.description:
Do you want to add **{name}** to Home Assistant?

Click Submit to start pairing.

battair_confirm.title: Add BattAir
battair_confirm.description:
Do you want to add **{name}** ({address}) to Home Assistant?

The pack is read from its Bluetooth broadcasts only, no pairing or connection is needed.

pair.title: Pair with {model}
pair.description:
Click Submit to start pairing.

If your device beeps and asks for confirmation (like the MASS2), **press any button on it within 30 seconds**. Devices without buttons (like the C4 Air or Power 200) accept the pairing automatically — no action needed.

show_device_info.title: Device Info

error.cannot_connect: Failed to connect to the device. Ensure it is powered on and in range.
error.pairing_failed: Pairing timed out. If your device has buttons, try again and press any button within 30 seconds. Otherwise make sure the device is powered on, in range and not connected to the ISDT app.

abort.no_devices_found: No ISDT device found. Ensure it is powered on and in range.

data_description.command_interval: Pause between two Bluetooth commands while polling (100–1000 ms, default 100). Raise it if charger values drop out every few seconds: on a weaker link some chargers skip commands that arrive too close together. Higher values make the readings update less often.
data_description.phantom_threshold: Adapter only. Above this a port is instantly reported as active (real charging). Below it the sustained-window logic kicks in. Set to 0 to disable phantom filtering entirely.
data_description.phantom_debounce: Adapter only. How long power must stay below the low threshold before an active port drops back to off. Bridges brief PD re-negotiation dips.
data_description.phantom_sustain: Adapter only. Slow chargers (e.g. electric toothbrushes at ~0.5 W) must stay continuously above the low threshold for this long before being reported as active. Samsung-style pad pulses (2–3 s) never reach this window, so they stay filtered.

standalone_card_installed.title: Standalone ISDT Charger Card is still installed
standalone_card_installed.description:
The ISDT Charger Card now ships with this integration and no longer needs to be installed separately.

A standalone copy of the card is still registered as a dashboard resource (`{url}`). Both copies register the same card element and only one of them wins, so the standalone copy can silently shadow the bundled, up-to-date card.

Please remove the standalone installation:

1. If installed via HACS: open HACS, find *ISDT Charger Card* and remove it (this also removes the dashboard resource).
2. If added manually: delete the resource under *Settings → Dashboards → Resources* and remove the file from your `www` folder.

Your dashboards keep working unchanged, the bundled card uses the same `custom:isdt-charger-card` type.

not_a_schedule.message: {entity_id} is not a schedule. Pick the Quiet hours switch or a port's Scheduled output switch.

set_schedule.name: Set schedule
set_schedule.description: Sets the days, and optionally the times and on/off, of the MASS2 quiet hours or of a USB-C port's scheduled output in one step. Any combination of days is possible. A start time after the end time runs past midnight; the same start and end time means the whole day.

days.name: Days
days.description: Weekdays on which the schedule starts. At least one day.

start_time.name: Start time
start_time.description: Start of the window (for a port: when it switches on). Unchanged if left out.

end_time.name: End time
end_time.description: End of the window (for a port: when it switches off). Unchanged if left out.

enabled.name: Enabled
enabled.description: Switch the schedule on or off. Unchanged if left out.
